# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 801
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/801
- **Title**: ci(security): SHA-pinned actions, explicit minimal permissions, dual-graph audit
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-796` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +440
- **Deletions**: -221
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T08:46:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-22T18:30:47Z

## PR Description

Closes #796 (SEC-08, MEDIUM).

## What

1. **SHA-pinned every third-party action ref** in `.github/workflows/*.yml` (213 call sites, 13 distinct actions). Each keeps its moving tag as a trailing comment (`actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`). SHAs resolved from the tag/branch heads live at PR time via the GitHub refs API. First-party repo-relative refs (`./.github/actions/...`) are exempt; the `dmtools-agents` factory `uses:` lines were already SHA-pinned and are byte-identical (machine-sm.yml / ai-teammate.yml touched only where noted below).
   - `ruby/setup-ruby@v1` is a moving BRANCH (no v1 tag exists) — pinned to the branch head `e8944e80` (v1.99 line).
2. **Explicit minimal top-level `permissions:` everywhere** (was implicit in 6 workflows). Jobs needing more keep their existing job-level grants.
   - `ai-teammate.yml`: the old comment forbade a permissions block because a read-only one startup_failure'd every factory call (live bisect 2026-09-18). The factory-teammate.yml (pinned ref) declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions **write**; a reusable workflow cannot raise rights above the caller, so the caller now mirrors exactly those scopes — the minimal consistent set. This is the caller↔reusable consistency the issue asks for; the factory call still validates.
   - `machine-sm.yml` already had a correct mirrored block — untouched.
3. **New `supply-chain` gate job** (every PR, no path gating, part of the aggregate Quality gate):
   - AC1: `scripts/check_action_pins.sh` fails any third-party ref that is not a full commit SHA (digest-pinned `docker://` refs would pass; nothing else).
   - AC2: lint asserts every workflow file has a top-level `permissions:` block (presence, not convention).
   - AC4 (REG): the job writes a `@v4` fixture and asserts the checker REJECTS it, plus a SHA-pinned fixture it must accept. Verified locally: bad fixture exit 1, clean exit 0, repo scan green.
4. **New `dep-audit` matrix job — both dependency graphs** (AC3):
   - `hosted`: `pubspec.yaml` alone — what `pub publish` ships and pub.dev consumers resolve;
   - `vendored`: `pubspec.yaml` + `pubspec_overrides.yaml` — local/CI/release binaries (dart_tui rides `vendor/dart_tui`).
   - The split is documented in the job summary; each leg also asserts from the resolved `pubspec.lock` that dart_tui actually came from its own source (`source: hosted` vs `source: path`), so a silently-collapsed split fails the leg. Both legs join the aggregate Quality gate.

## Verification

- All 21 workflow YAMLs parse (ruby yaml); `bash -n` clean on the new script.
- `bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh` → OK over the full tree (workflows + composite actions).
- Fixture REG run locally: `@v4` fixture fails (exit 1), SHA-pinned fixture passes, repo scan passes.
- AC2 lint loop over all workflows: no missing blocks.

## Notes / gaps

- Dependabot/Renovate is listed in the issue contract ("keeps them current") but this repo has no package-ecosystem config for actions and adding one was not requested in the Change scope — the trailing tag comments make manual bumping a one-liner; happy to add a `github-actions` Dependabot config as a follow-up if wanted.
- `actions/upload-artifact@v7` (build-macos.yml) and the other major versions were pinned as-found; upgrades are a separate concern.

{
  "key": "pr-801",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "ci(security): SHA-pinned actions, explicit minimal permissions, dual-graph audit",
    "description": "Closes #796 (SEC-08, MEDIUM).

## What

1. **SHA-pinned every third-party action ref** in `.github/workflows/*.yml` (213 call sites, 13 distinct actions). Each keeps its moving tag as a trailing comment (`actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`). SHAs resolved from the tag/branch heads live at PR time via the GitHub refs API. First-party repo-relative refs (`./.github/actions/...`) are exempt; the `dmtools-agents` factory `uses:` lines were already SHA-pinned and are byte-identical (machine-sm.yml / ai-teammate.yml touched only where noted below).
   - `ruby/setup-ruby@v1` is a moving BRANCH (no v1 tag exists) — pinned to the branch head `e8944e80` (v1.99 line).
2. **Explicit minimal top-level `permissions:` everywhere** (was implicit in 6 workflows). Jobs needing more keep their existing job-level grants.
   - `ai-teammate.yml`: the old comment forbade a permissions block because a read-only one startup_failure'd every factory call (live bisect 2026-09-18). The factory-teammate.yml (pinned ref) declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions **write**; a reusable workflow cannot raise rights above the caller, so the caller now mirrors exactly those scopes — the minimal consistent set. This is the caller↔reusable consistency the issue asks for; the factory call still validates.
   - `machine-sm.yml` already had a correct mirrored block — untouched.
3. **New `supply-chain` gate job** (every PR, no path gating, part of the aggregate Quality gate):
   - AC1: `scripts/check_action_pins.sh` fails any third-party ref that is not a full commit SHA (digest-pinned `docker://` refs would pass; nothing else).
   - AC2: lint asserts every workflow file has a top-level `permissions:` block (presence, not convention).
   - AC4 (REG): the job writes a `@v4` fixture and asserts the checker REJECTS it, plus a SHA-pinned fixture it must accept. Verified locally: bad fixture exit 1, clean exit 0, repo scan green.
4. **New `dep-audit` matrix job — both dependency graphs** (AC3):
   - `hosted`: `pubspec.yaml` alone — what `pub publish` ships and pub.dev consumers resolve;
   - `vendored`: `pubspec.yaml` + `pubspec_overrides.yaml` — local/CI/release binaries (dart_tui rides `vendor/dart_tui`).
   - The split is documented in the job summary; each leg also asserts from the resolved `pubspec.lock` that dart_tui actually came from its own source (`source: hosted` vs `source: path`), so a silently-collapsed split fails the leg. Both legs join the aggregate Quality gate.

## Verification

- All 21 workflow YAMLs parse (ruby yaml); `bash -n` clean on the new script.
- `bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh` → OK over the full tree (workflows + composite actions).
- Fixture REG run locally: `@v4` fixture fails (exit 1), SHA-pinned fixture passes, repo scan passes.
- AC2 lint loop over all workflows: no missing blocks.

## Notes / gaps

- Dependabot/Renovate is listed in the issue contract ("keeps them current") but this repo has no package-ecosystem config for actions and adding one was not requested in the Change scope — the trailing tag comments make manual bumping a one-liner; happy to add a `github-actions` Dependabot config as a follow-up if wanted.
- `actions/upload-artifact@v7` (build-macos.yml) and the other major versions were pinned as-found; upgrades are a separate concern."
  }
}

blocks.text:
+      contents: read
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        graph: [hosted, vendored]
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
+      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
+        with:
+          sdk: stable
+      # Hosted leg = exactly what pub.dev consumers resolve; the overrides
+      # file never ships, so it must not bend this graph.
+      - name: Park vendored overrides (hosted leg)
+        if: matrix.graph == 'hosted'
+        run: mv pubspec_overrides.yaml pubspec_overrides.yaml.vendored
+      - run: dart pub get
+      - name: Audit the ${{ matrix.graph }} dependency graph
+        run: |
+          {
+            echo "### Dependency audit — \`${{ matrix.graph }}\` graph"
+            echo ""
+            echo "This repo resolves TWO dependency graphs (SEC-08):"
+            echo "- **hosted** — \`pubspec.yaml\` alone: what \`pub publish\` ships and pub.dev consumers resolve (dart_tui hosted)."
+            echo "- **vendored** — \`pubspec.yaml\` + \`pubspec_overrides.yaml\`: local dev, CI and the release binaries (dart_tui rides \`vendor/dart_tui\`)."
+            echo ""
+            echo "An audit of one says nothing about the other, so both are audited on every run. Resolved graph:"
+            echo ""
+          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+          dart pub deps --style=compact | tee /tmp/graph.txt >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
+          {
+            echo ""
+            echo "Outdated direct dependencies (informational):"
+            echo '```'
+            dart pub outdated
+            echo '```'
+          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
+          # The split must be REAL: each leg resolves dart_tui from its own
+          # source, read from the resolved pubspec.lock.
+          lock_block=$(grep -A7 '^  dart_tui:' pubspec.lock)
+          echo "$lock_block"
+          case "${{ matrix.graph }}" in
+            hosted)
+              if echo "$lock_block" | grep -q 'source: path'; then
+                echo "::error::hosted graph resolved the vendored dart_tui fork"
+                exit 1
+              fi
+              echo "$lock_block" | grep -q 'source: hosted'
+              ;;
+            vendored)
+              echo "$lock_block" | grep -q 'source: path' || {
+                echo "::error::vendored graph did not resolve dart_tui from vendor/dart_tui"
+                exit 1
+              }
+              ;;
+          esac
+          echo "${{ matrix.graph }} graph audit OK"

Now I have the full diff. Let me now do the deep review. Key things to check:

1. **ai-teammate.yml permissions change** — the old comment said NO permissions block because a read-only one startup_failure'd. The new one grants `contents: write, issues: write, pull-requests: write, actions: write` at the top level of the **ai-teammate.yml** workflow, which runs on issue events (and workflow_dispatch?). This means every job in this workflow now gets these write permissions... wait, actually the reusable workflow call itself. Let me read the full ai-teammate.yml to understand.

2. **The supply-chain gate job** in ci.yml:
   - `needs: changes` — and there's no `if:` condition. The changes job classifies paths. Wait, but does the `changes` job have an `if` that could skip? Note: `supply-chain` runs on every PR, but what about main pushes and tags? The `quality-gate` needs supply-chain; quality-gate is presumably `if: always()`. But the supply-chain job itself needs `changes`, and the changes job has outputs. If supply-chain has `needs: changes` but no `if:`, it will always run. That's fine. But does supply-chain check the trigger? It says "Runs on EVERY PR — no path gating". But is it running on main/tag pushes too? That's fine.
   
   However — an important detail: the `changes` job on non-PR events runs with `fetch-depth: 0` etc. Fine.

   - AC2 lint: `grep -q '^permissions:'` — checks every `.github/workflows/*.yml` has a top-level permissions block. But it does NOT check `.github/workflows/*.yaml` — the checker script handles both `*.yml` and `*.yaml`, but the AC2 inline lint only globs `*.yml`. If a workflow file used `.yaml` extension, the AC2 check would silently miss it. Minor inconsistency. Also AC2 doesn't check composite action metadata files — not required by AC2 though.

3. **check_action_pins.sh**:
   - `set -eu` — with the `refs=$(grep ... ) || true` pattern; fine.
   - The regex `'^[[:space:]]*(-[[:space:]]+)?uses:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]+'` — matches lines that start with optional whitespace, then optionally `- `, then `uses:`. But a `uses:` key could appear at a nested level with `- uses:` — covered. What about `uses: |` multiline? Not typical.
   - **Bug potential**: A YAML file containing a line like `foo: bar` followed by text "uses:" inside a string or comment. E.g., a comment line `# uses: actions/checkout@v4` — the grep requires the line to start with optional whitespace and `-` then `uses:`, so `# uses:` won't match since `#` isn't allowed. Good.
   - What about `uses:` with quoted ref `"actions/checkout@v4"`? The `[^[:space:]]+` captures `"actions/checkout@v4"` including quotes; then `sha="${ref##*@}"` → `v4"` which fails the 40-hex check → flagged as violation. Good (fails closed).
   - What about uppercase hex SHA? `?????` pattern of exactly 40 chars matches any character, not just hex! The case pattern `????` is 40 question marks — that matches ANY 40-character string, not just hex! So `actions/checkout@THIS_IS_A_40_CHAR_LONG_STRING!` would pass. Wait, let me count: 40 question marks match any 40 chars. So a branch named e.g. `refs/heads/abc...` of exactly 40 chars would pass. Is that a real security issue? A mutable 40-char branch name would pass the checker. E.g., `someone/action@main-branch-name-40-chars-xxxxxxxx`. Hmm, this is a real correctness gap in the checker: it doesn't validate hex. The comment says "40-hex commit SHA" but the pattern doesn't enforce hex. This is a genuine finding — the gate can be bypassed by any 40-char mutable ref. Severity: IMPORTANT (defense-in-depth gate has a hole; not directly exploitable in this repo since it self-scans, but the checker's whole purpose is validation). Actually, let me think: the checker is applied to the repo's own workflows. The threat model is a PR adding an unpinned action; the gate would catch it — unless the ref is a 40-char non-hex string. An attacker who can modify workflows already has code exec in CI. The gate is advisory. So severity: IMPORTANT.
   
   - `docker://` handling: only `docker://` refs with digest pass. OK.
   - The exemption `./*` — first-party `./.github/actions/...` and `./.github/workflows/...`. But what about `./` refs pointing to... they're repo-relative, fine.
   - **Missing scan coverage**: The repo scan covers `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `*.yaml`, and `.github/actions/*/action.yml`. What about nested composite actions deeper than one level (`.github/actions/foo/bar/action.yml`)? Possibly. Also what about `action.yml` files elsewhere in the repo (e.g. `factory-agents/`, `js-ext-registry/`, or vendor dirs)? Let me check if there are other action.yml files in the repo that contain `uses:`. Also Dockerfiles? The AC1 is about GitHub Actions refs. Let me check for other action.yaml/action.yml in the repo.

4. **dep-audit job**:
   - The hosted leg does `mv pubspec_overrides.yaml pubspec_overrides.yaml.vendored` — wait, but does `dart pub get` care? Fine. But: the hosted leg asserts `grep -q 'source: hosted'` on the lock_block — `lock_block=$(grep -A7 '^  dart_tui:' pubspec.lock)`. If grep finds nothing, `lock_block` is empty, and under `set -e`... wait, this is inside a `run: |` block — bash with `-e`? GitHub Actions run steps use `bash -e` by default (actually `bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail` if shell: bash, or `sh -e` default). The default shell on Linux for run steps is `bash -e` (without pipefail unless specified). Hmm — actually GitHub defaults: for `run` steps on Linux/macOS, the shell is `bash -e {0}`. So `set -e` semantics apply. But `lock_block=$(grep ...)` — if grep fails (no match), the assignment's exit status is grep's (1) → step fails. That would fail with a confusing error but still fails closed. In the hosted leg, if dart_tui is missing from lock, step fails. OK, fails closed either way.
   - `dart pub outdated` — appends to step summary with `|| true` on the group. Note `dart pub outdated` returns exit code 0 normally, but if there are outdated deps? `dart pub outdated` exits 0 even when outdated packages exist (it's informational). Fine.

   - One concern: the hosted leg renames `pubspec_overrides.yaml` — but the workspace is not restored; harmless in ephemeral CI.

If pubspec.yaml itself has other path deps (e.g., a `packages/fa_ui` path dep?), then hosted pub get would fail. Actually the PR says validation CI went red — maybe because of this. Edge case: if dart_tui entry is followed within 7 lines by another package whose source is `path`, then hosted leg's `grep -q 'source: path'` would false-positive fail. Not likely, minor.

Note one subtlety in the dep-audit job: in the vendored leg the `-A7` window catches `  equatable:` — the next package's key line. If `equatable`'s entry had `source: path`... it doesn't matter for the vendored assertion (positive check). For the HOSTED assertion, the negative check `grep -q 'source: path'` — the window includes the next package header `  equatable:` plus lines into its entry (dependency/description/name/sha256/url/source). If the package right after dart_tui in alphabetical order had `source: path`... In the hosted graph there are no path packages after dart_tui in the window (equatable is hosted). But in dev deps there are path packages: fa_llm_mock, xterm. Alphabetical order in lock: dart_tui is followed by equatable — safe today. But it's a fragile 7-line window (could false-fail if lockfile ordering shifts, e.g. a package named `dart_tui_x` … no—window is fixed at 7 lines after the key). The next entry's `source:` line lands at exactly the 7th line? Let me count from the actual lock:

    description:       <- 2

    version: "2.1.0"   <- 7

blocks.text:
# SM CI Gate — the pull_request bridge over dispatch-only CI.
#
# GitHub does not associate workflow_dispatch runs with pull requests:
# the SM-dispatched CI run registers green check runs on the head SHA,
# but branch protection's required checks ("Quality gate", "JS engine
# integration (quickjs-ng)", "Binaries smoke gate") only read
# PR-ASSOCIATED check runs — they would sit "expected" forever and every
# merge would 405.
#
# This bridge IS the PR association. It runs per head (pull_request
# event — cheap: one poll job + three mirror steps, no CI matrix), waits
# for the SM-dispatched CI run (workflow_dispatch on this exact head
# SHA) and mirrors its conclusion under the required check names. The
# expensive matrix still runs ONLY when the SM dispatches it.
#
# Failure modes: SM broken / never dispatches -> the waiter times out
# after 85 min and the mirrors go red (human signal). Dispatched run
# red -> mirrors red. Cancelled/skipped dispatched runs are concurrency
# debris, never a verdict: the selection only honors terminal
# success/failure conclusions and keeps polling. A cancelled WAITER
# (re-run debris) leaves the mirrors skipped — the superseding attempt
# owns the verdict. Draft PRs skip the waiter AND the mirrors.

name: 'SM CI Gate'

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

concurrency:
  group: sm-gate-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read

jobs:
  sm-validation:
    name: 'sm-validation (waits for the SM-dispatched CI run)'
    if: ${{ !github.event.pull_request.draft }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    outputs:
      conclusion: ${{ steps.wait.outputs.conclusion }}
    steps:
      - name: Wait for the dispatched CI run on this head
        id: wait
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
        run: |
          # Bounded dispatch-watch, house dialect (cf. the pub.dev watch in
          # ci.yml): deadline=$((SECONDS + N)), 30 s ticks, visible poll
          # lines, loud ::error:: on expiry.
          #
          # Verdict = the NEWEST TERMINAL dispatched run for this head SHA:
          #   fast (never eats the tolerance): failure timed_out
          #                                    startup_failure action_required
          #                                    — red in seconds, even while
          #                                    a rerun is in flight
          #   gated on nothing-pending:        success — an in-flight rerun
          #                                    outranks an older green, but
          #                                    a pending run wedged past
          #                                    STALE_PENDING stops blocking
          #                                    (staleness cap -> verdict)
          #   never a verdict:                 cancelled skipped neutral
          #                                    (and null) — concurrency-wave
          #                                    debris; the SM re-dispatches
          #                                    on its next tick
          # Degraded paths are surfaced, never silent: api-poll failures
          # warn (1st + every 10th) and count toward the deadline error, a
          # stale pending run escalates to the summary once.
          set -euo pipefail
          WAIT="${WAIT_SECONDS:-5100}"                    # 85 min: slow pool +
                                                          # SM tick (10 min)
                                                          # must not outlive
                                                          # the waiter (44
                                                          # min flapped)
          STALE_PENDING="${STALE_PENDING_SECONDS:-2400}"  # 40 min: wedged cap
          deadline=$((SECONDS + WAIT))
          escalated=0 api_fails=0
          note() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"; }
          # Branch names are attacker-influenced and may legally contain
          # backticks, pipes and angle brackets — strip them once so the ref
          # can never break out of a markdown code span (or inject markup)
          # in the job summary.
          ref_display="${REF//[\`|<>]/_}"

          # Emits "verdict|pending_count|oldest_pending_epoch" — empty on
          # api/jq failure (counted, so a broken API stays distinguishable
          # from a slow pool).
          poll_api() {
            gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?event=workflow_dispatch&head_sha=${SHA}&per_page=30" \
              --jq '([.workflow_runs[] | select(.status != "completed") | (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)] | min // 0) as $oldest
                   | ([.workflow_runs[] | select(.conclusion == "success" or .conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "timed_out" or .conclusion == "startup_failure" or .conclusion == "action_required")] | first | .conclusion // "") as $c
                   | ([.workflow_runs[] | select(.status != "completed")] | length) as $p
                   | "\($c)|\($p)|\($oldest)"' 2>/dev/null
          }

          while [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$deadline" ]; do
            out="$(poll_api || true)"
            if [ -z "$out" ]; then
              api_fails=$((api_fails + 1))
              if [ "$api_fails" -eq 1 ] || [ $((api_fails % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then
                echo "::warning::dispatch-run poll failed ${api_fails}x (api/jq) — continuing"
              fi
              if [ "$api_fails" -eq 1 ]; then
                note "| :warning: dispatch-watch: run poll failed ${api_fails}x — verdicts may lag reality."
              fi
              sleep 30
              continue
            fi
            c="${out%%|*}"; rest="${out#*|}"; pending="${rest%%|*}"; oldest="${rest##*|}"
            age=0
            if [ "$pending" -gt 0 ]; then age=$(( $(date +%s) - oldest )); fi
            echo "poll: verdict='${c:-none}' pending=$pending pending_age=${age}s (t=${SECONDS}s)"

            # Fast terminal verdicts — red stays red in seconds.
            case "$c" in
              failure|timed_out|startup_failure|action_required)
                echo "conclusion=$c" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                echo "SM-dispatched CI run verdict: $c"
                exit 0 ;;
            esac

            stale=0
            if [ "$pending" -gt 0 ] && [ "$age" -ge "$STALE_PENDING" ]; then stale=1; fi

            # Green: only when nothing is pending, or the pending run is
            # wedged past the staleness cap.
            if [ "$c" = "success" ] && { [ "$pending" -eq 0 ] || [ "$stale" -eq 1 ]; }; then
              if [ "$stale" -eq 1 ]; then
                note "| :warning: dispatched run pending ${age}s (wedged?) — accepted older verdict \`success\`."
                echo "SM-dispatched CI run verdict: success (stale pending ${age}s ignored)"
              else
                echo "SM-dispatched CI run verdict: success"
              fi
              echo "conclusion=success" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi

            # Stale pending with no verdict to fall back on: escalate once,
            # keep polling — the slow-pool signal stays honest.
            if [ "$stale" -eq 1 ] && [ "$escalated" -eq 0 ]; then
              escalated=1
              note "| :warning: dispatched run pending ${age}s with no terminal verdict on \`${ref_display}\` — wedged queue? Polling continues until the deadline."
              echo "::warning::dispatched run pending ${age}s with no terminal verdict — watch continues"
            fi

            sleep 30
          done

          echo "::error::SM-dispatched validation did not conclude within $((WAIT / 60)) min (api failures: ${api_fails}) — SM tick broken or queue stalled"
          note "| :x: dispatch-watch: no verdict within $((WAIT / 60)) min on \`${ref_display}\` — api_failures=${api_fails}. SM tick broken or queue stalled."
          exit 1

  quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    needs: sm-validation
    if: …

Now the critical interaction with this PR's changes to ci.yml: **the new `supply-chain` and `dep-audit` jobs and the quality-gate's expanded needs** — when the SM dispatches ci.yml via workflow_dispatch, do `supply-chain` and `dep-audit` run? blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
#
#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      (github.event.inputs.pr != '' &&
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · pr-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.pr) ||
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · gh-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# Explicit top-level permissions, mirroring the pinned factory's own block
# (factory-teammate.yml declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions
# write). A reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the caller, so the
# caller must grant at least what the callee declares — an explicit
# read-only block here made every call fail validation with
# startup_failure (live bisect, 2026-09-18); this mirror is the minimal
# consistent set (SEC-08, #796).
permissions:
  contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
  issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
  actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
  gate:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in
            workflow_dispatch)
              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            issues)
              # Assignment-driven loop: a fresh `assigned` event (human
              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.
              # POLICY (#693 steering): dev fires ONLY when ai-teammate is
              # the sole assignee — any human assignee owns the issue and
              # the machine stands by for reviews instead (review paths:
              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                else
                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
                fi
              else
                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              fi
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
          esac
          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

  factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@8c02d860813f520d8c43af8c56f3f56452153295
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 8c02d860813f520d8c43af8c56f3f56452153295
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 801
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/801
- **Title**: ci(security): SHA-pinned actions, explicit minimal permissions, dual-graph audit
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-796` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +440
- **Deletions**: -221
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T08:46:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-22T18:30:47Z

## PR Description

Closes #796 (SEC-08, MEDIUM).

## What

1. **SHA-pinned every third-party action ref** in `.github/workflows/*.yml` (213 call sites, 13 distinct actions). Each keeps its moving tag as a trailing comment (`actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`). SHAs resolved from the tag/branch heads live at PR time via the GitHub refs API. First-party repo-relative refs (`./.github/actions/...`) are exempt; the `dmtools-agents` factory `uses:` lines were already SHA-pinned and are byte-identical (machine-sm.yml / ai-teammate.yml touched only where noted below).
   - `ruby/setup-ruby@v1` is a moving BRANCH (no v1 tag exists) — pinned to the branch head `e8944e80` (v1.99 line).
2. **Explicit minimal top-level `permissions:` everywhere** (was implicit in 6 workflows). Jobs needing more keep their existing job-level grants.
   - `ai-teammate.yml`: the old comment forbade a permissions block because a read-only one startup_failure'd every factory call (live bisect 2026-09-18). The factory-teammate.yml (pinned ref) declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions **write**; a reusable workflow cannot raise rights above the caller, so the caller now mirrors exactly those scopes — the minimal consistent set. This is the caller↔reusable consistency the issue asks for; the factory call still validates.
   - `machine-sm.yml` already had a correct mirrored block — untouched.
3. **New `supply-chain` gate job** (every PR, no path gating, part of the aggregate Quality gate):
   - AC1: `scripts/check_action_pins.sh` fails any third-party ref that is not a full commit SHA (digest-pinned `docker://` refs would pass; nothing else).
   - AC2: lint asserts every workflow file has a top-level `permissions:` block (presence, not convention).
   - AC4 (REG): the job writes a `@v4` fixture and asserts the checker REJECTS it, plus a SHA-pinned fixture it must accept. Verified locally: bad fixture exit 1, clean exit 0, repo scan green.
4. **New `dep-audit` matrix job — both dependency graphs** (AC3):
   - `hosted`: `pubspec.yaml` alone — what `pub publish` ships and pub.dev consumers resolve;
   - `vendored`: `pubspec.yaml` + `pubspec_overrides.yaml` — local/CI/release binaries (dart_tui rides `vendor/dart_tui`).
   - The split is documented in the job summary; each leg also asserts from the resolved `pubspec.lock` that dart_tui actually came from its own source (`source: hosted` vs `source: path`), so a silently-collapsed split fails the leg. Both legs join the aggregate Quality gate.

## Verification

- All 21 workflow YAMLs parse (ruby yaml); `bash -n` clean on the new script.
- `bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh` → OK over the full tree (workflows + composite actions).
- Fixture REG run locally: `@v4` fixture fails (exit 1), SHA-pinned fixture passes, repo scan passes.
- AC2 lint loop over all workflows: no missing blocks.

## Notes / gaps

- Dependabot/Renovate is listed in the issue contract ("keeps them current") but this repo has no package-ecosystem config for actions and adding one was not requested in the Change scope — the trailing tag comments make manual bumping a one-liner; happy to add a `github-actions` Dependabot config as a follow-up if wanted.
- `actions/upload-artifact@v7` (build-macos.yml) and the other major versions were pinned as-found; upgrades are a separate concern.

{
  "key": "pr-801",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "ci(security): SHA-pinned actions, explicit minimal permissions, dual-graph audit",
    "description": "Closes #796 (SEC-08, MEDIUM).

## What

1. **SHA-pinned every third-party action ref** in `.github/workflows/*.yml` (213 call sites, 13 distinct actions). Each keeps its moving tag as a trailing comment (`actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`). SHAs resolved from the tag/branch heads live at PR time via the GitHub refs API. First-party repo-relative refs (`./.github/actions/...`) are exempt; the `dmtools-agents` factory `uses:` lines were already SHA-pinned and are byte-identical (machine-sm.yml / ai-teammate.yml touched only where noted below).
   - `ruby/setup-ruby@v1` is a moving BRANCH (no v1 tag exists) — pinned to the branch head `e8944e80` (v1.99 line).
2. **Explicit minimal top-level `permissions:` everywhere** (was implicit in 6 workflows). Jobs needing more keep their existing job-level grants.
   - `ai-teammate.yml`: the old comment forbade a permissions block because a read-only one startup_failure'd every factory call (live bisect 2026-09-18). The factory-teammate.yml (pinned ref) declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions **write**; a reusable workflow cannot raise rights above the caller, so the caller now mirrors exactly those scopes — the minimal consistent set. This is the caller↔reusable consistency the issue asks for; the factory call still validates.
   - `machine-sm.yml` already had a correct mirrored block — untouched.
3. **New `supply-chain` gate job** (every PR, no path gating, part of the aggregate Quality gate):
   - AC1: `scripts/check_action_pins.sh` fails any third-party ref that is not a full commit SHA (digest-pinned `docker://` refs would pass; nothing else).
   - AC2: lint asserts every workflow file has a top-level `permissions:` block (presence, not convention).
   - AC4 (REG): the job writes a `@v4` fixture and asserts the checker REJECTS it, plus a SHA-pinned fixture it must accept. Verified locally: bad fixture exit 1, clean exit 0, repo scan green.
4. **New `dep-audit` matrix job — both dependency graphs** (AC3):
   - `hosted`: `pubspec.yaml` alone — what `pub publish` ships and pub.dev consumers resolve;
   - `vendored`: `pubspec.yaml` + `pubspec_overrides.yaml` — local/CI/release binaries (dart_tui rides `vendor/dart_tui`).
   - The split is documented in the job summary; each leg also asserts from the resolved `pubspec.lock` that dart_tui actually came from its own source (`source: hosted` vs `source: path`), so a silently-collapsed split fails the leg. Both legs join the aggregate Quality gate.

## Verification

- All 21 workflow YAMLs parse (ruby yaml); `bash -n` clean on the new script.
- `bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh` → OK over the full tree (workflows + composite actions).
- Fixture REG run locally: `@v4` fixture fails (exit 1), SHA-pinned fixture passes, repo scan passes.
- AC2 lint loop over all workflows: no missing blocks.

## Notes / gaps

- Dependabot/Renovate is listed in the issue contract ("keeps them current") but this repo has no package-ecosystem config for actions and adding one was not requested in the Change scope — the trailing tag comments make manual bumping a one-liner; happy to add a `github-actions` Dependabot config as a follow-up if wanted.
- `actions/upload-artifact@v7` (build-macos.yml) and the other major versions were pinned as-found; upgrades are a separate concern."
  }
}

+      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
+        with:
+          sdk: stable
+      # Hosted leg = exactly what pub.dev consumers resolve; the overrides
+      # file never ships, so it must not bend this graph.
+      - name: Park vendored overrides (hosted leg)
+        if: matrix.graph == 'hosted'
+        run: mv pubspec_overrides.yaml pubspec_overrides.yaml.vendored
+      - run: dart pub get
+      - name: Audit the ${{ matrix.graph }} dependency graph
+        run: |
+          {
+            echo "### Dependency audit — \`${{ matrix.graph }}\` graph"
+            echo ""
+            echo "This repo resolves TWO dependency graphs (SEC-08):"
+            echo "- **hosted** — \`pubspec.yaml\` alone: what \`pub publish\` ships and pub.dev consumers resolve (dart_tui hosted)."
+            echo "- **vendored** — \`pubspec.yaml\` + \`pubspec_overrides.yaml\`: local dev, CI and the release binaries (dart_tui rides \`vendor/dart_tui\`)."
+            echo ""
+            echo "An audit of one says nothing about the other, so both are audited on every run. Resolved graph:"
+            echo ""
+          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+          dart pub deps --style=compact | tee /tmp/graph.txt >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
+          {
+            echo ""
+            echo "Outdated direct dependencies (informational):"
+            echo '```'
+            dart pub outdated
+            echo '```'
+          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
+          # The split must be REAL: each leg resolves dart_tui from its own
+          # source, read from the resolved pubspec.lock.
+          lock_block=$(grep -A7 '^  dart_tui:' pubspec.lock)
+          echo "$lock_block"
+          case "${{ matrix.graph }}" in
+            hosted)
+              if echo "$lock_block" | grep -q 'source: path'; then
+                echo "::error::hosted graph resolved the vendored dart_tui fork"
+                exit 1
+              fi
+              echo "$lock_block" | grep -q 'source: hosted'
+              ;;
+            vendored)
+              echo "$lock_block" | grep -q 'source: path' || {
+                echo "::error::vendored graph did not resolve dart_tui from vendor/dart_tui"
+                exit 1
+              }
+              ;;
+          esac
+          echo "${{ matrix.graph }} graph audit OK"

Now I have the full diff. Let me now do the deep review. Key things to check:

1. **ai-teammate.yml permissions change** — the old comment said NO permissions block because a read-only one startup_failure'd. The new one grants `contents: write, issues: write, pull-requests: write, actions: write` at the top level of the **ai-teammate.yml** workflow, which runs on issue events (and workflow_dispatch?). This means every job in this workflow now gets these write permissions... wait, actually the reusable workflow call itself. Let me read the full ai-teammate.yml to understand.

2. **The supply-chain gate job** in ci.yml:
   - `needs: changes` — and there's no `if:` condition. The changes job classifies paths. Wait, but does the `changes` job have an `if` that could skip? Note: `supply-chain` runs on every PR, but what about main pushes and tags? The `quality-gate` needs supply-chain; quality-gate is presumably `if: always()`. But the supply-chain job itself needs `changes`, and the changes job has outputs. If supply-chain has `needs: changes` but no `if:`, it will always run. That's fine. But does supply-chain check the trigger? It says "Runs on EVERY PR — no path gating". But is it running on main/tag pushes too? That's fine.
   
   However — an important detail: the `changes` job on non-PR events runs with `fetch-depth: 0` etc. Fine.

   - AC2 lint: `grep -q '^permissions:'` — checks every `.github/workflows/*.yml` has a top-level permissions block. But it does NOT check `.github/workflows/*.yaml` — the checker script handles both `*.yml` and `*.yaml`, but the AC2 inline lint only globs `*.yml`. If a workflow file used `.yaml` extension, the AC2 check would silently miss it. Minor inconsistency. Also AC2 doesn't check composite action metadata files — not required by AC2 though.

3. **check_action_pins.sh**:
   - `set -eu` — with the `refs=$(grep ... ) || true` pattern; fine.
   - The regex `'^[[:space:]]*(-[[:space:]]+)?uses:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]+'` — matches lines that start with optional whitespace, then optionally `- `, then `uses:`. But a `uses:` key could appear at a nested level with `- uses:` — covered. What about `uses: |` multiline? Not typical.
   - **Bug potential**: A YAML file containing a line like `foo: bar` followed by text "uses:" inside a string or comment. E.g., a comment line `# uses: actions/checkout@v4` — the grep requires the line to start with optional whitespace and `-` then `uses:`, so `# uses:` won't match since `#` isn't allowed. Good.
   - What about `uses:` with quoted ref `"actions/checkout@v4"`? The `[^[:space:]]+` captures `"actions/checkout@v4"` including quotes; then `sha="${ref##*@}"` → `v4"` which fails the 40-hex check → flagged as violation. Good (fails closed).
   - What about uppercase hex SHA? `?????` pattern of exactly 40 chars matches any character, not just hex! The case pattern `????` is 40 question marks — that matches ANY 40-character string, not just hex! So `actions/checkout@THIS_IS_A_40_CHAR_LONG_STRING!` would pass. Wait, let me count: 40 question marks match any 40 chars. So a branch named e.g. `refs/heads/abc...` of exactly 40 chars would pass. Is that a real security issue? A mutable 40-char branch name would pass the checker. E.g., `someone/action@main-branch-name-40-chars-xxxxxxxx`. Hmm, this is a real correctness gap in the checker: it doesn't validate hex. The comment says "40-hex commit SHA" but the pattern doesn't enforce hex. This is a genuine finding — the gate can be bypassed by any 40-char mutable ref. Severity: IMPORTANT (defense-in-depth gate has a hole; not directly exploitable in this repo since it self-scans, but the checker's whole purpose is validation). Actually, let me think: the checker is applied to the repo's own workflows. The threat model is a PR adding an unpinned action; the gate would catch it — unless the ref is a 40-char non-hex string. An attacker who can modify workflows already has code exec in CI. The gate is advisory. So severity: IMPORTANT.
   
   - `docker://` handling: only `docker://` refs with digest pass. OK.
   - The exemption `./*` — first-party `./.github/actions/...` and `./.github/workflows/...`. But what about `./` refs pointing to... they're repo-relative, fine.
   - **Missing scan coverage**: The repo scan covers `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `*.yaml`, and `.github/actions/*/action.yml`. What about nested composite actions deeper than one level (`.github/actions/foo/bar/action.yml`)? Possibly. Also what about `action.yml` files elsewhere in the repo (e.g. `factory-agents/`, `js-ext-registry/`, or vendor dirs)? Let me check if there are other action.yml files in the repo that contain `uses:`. Also Dockerfiles? The AC1 is about GitHub Actions refs. Let me check for other action.yaml/action.yml in the repo.

4. **dep-audit job**:
   - The hosted leg does `mv pubspec_overrides.yaml pubspec_overrides.yaml.vendored` — wait, but does `dart pub get` care? Fine. # SM CI Gate — the pull_request bridge over dispatch-only CI.
#
# GitHub does not associate workflow_dispatch runs with pull requests:

blocks.text:
# SM CI Gate — the pull_request bridge over dispatch-only CI.
#
# GitHub does not associate workflow_dispatch runs with pull requests:
# the SM-dispatched CI run registers green check runs on the head SHA,
# but branch protection's required checks ("Quality gate", "JS engine
# integration (quickjs-ng)", "Binaries smoke gate") only read
# PR-ASSOCIATED check runs — they would sit "expected" forever and every
# merge would 405.
#
# This bridge IS the PR association. It runs per head (pull_request
# event — cheap: one poll job + three mirror steps, no CI matrix), waits
# for the SM-dispatched CI run (workflow_dispatch on this exact head
# SHA) and mirrors its conclusion under the required check names. The
# expensive matrix still runs ONLY when the SM dispatches it.
#
# Failure modes: SM broken / never dispatches -> the waiter times out
# after 85 min and the mirrors go red (human signal). Dispatched run
# red -> mirrors red. Cancelled/skipped dispatched runs are concurrency
# debris, never a verdict: the selection only honors terminal
# success/failure conclusions and keeps polling. A cancelled WAITER
# (re-run debris) leaves the mirrors skipped — the superseding attempt
# owns the verdict. Draft PRs skip the waiter AND the mirrors.

name: 'SM CI Gate'

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

concurrency:
  group: sm-gate-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read

jobs:
  sm-validation:
    name: 'sm-validation (waits for the SM-dispatched CI run)'
    if: ${{ !github.event.pull_request.draft }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    outputs:
      conclusion: ${{ steps.wait.outputs.conclusion }}
    steps:
      - name: Wait for the dispatched CI run on this head
        id: wait
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
        run: |
          # Bounded dispatch-watch, house dialect (cf. the pub.dev watch in
          # ci.yml): deadline=$((SECONDS + N)), 30 s ticks, visible poll
          # lines, loud ::error:: on expiry.
          #
          # Verdict = the NEWEST TERMINAL dispatched run for this head SHA:
          #   fast (never eats the tolerance): failure timed_out
          #                                    startup_failure action_required
          #                                    — red in seconds, even while
          #                                    a rerun is in flight
          #   gated on nothing-pending:        success — an in-flight rerun
          #                                    outranks an older green, but
          #                                    a pending run wedged past
          #                                    STALE_PENDING stops blocking
          #                                    (staleness cap -> verdict)
          #   never a verdict:                 cancelled skipped neutral
          #                                    (and null) — concurrency-wave
          #                                    debris; the SM re-dispatches
          #                                    on its next tick
          # Degraded paths are surfaced, never silent: api-poll failures
          # warn (1st + every 10th) and count toward the deadline error, a
          # stale pending run escalates to the summary once.
          set -euo pipefail
          WAIT="${WAIT_SECONDS:-5100}"                    # 85 min: slow pool +
                                                          # SM tick (10 min)
                                                          # must not outlive
                                                          # the waiter (44
                                                          # min flapped)
          STALE_PENDING="${STALE_PENDING_SECONDS:-2400}"  # 40 min: wedged cap
          deadline=$((SECONDS + WAIT))
          escalated=0 api_fails=0
          note() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"; }
          # Branch names are attacker-influenced and may legally contain
          # backticks, pipes and angle brackets — strip them once so the ref
          # can never break out of a markdown code span (or inject markup)
          # in the job summary.
          ref_display="${REF//[\`|<>]/_}"

          # Emits "verdict|pending_count|oldest_pending_epoch" — empty on
          # api/jq failure (counted, so a broken API stays distinguishable
          # from a slow pool).
          poll_api() {
            gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?event=workflow_dispatch&head_sha=${SHA}&per_page=30" \
              --jq '([.workflow_runs[] | select(.status != "completed") | (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)] | min // 0) as $oldest
                   | ([.workflow_runs[] | select(.conclusion == "success" or .conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "timed_out" or .conclusion == "startup_failure" or .conclusion == "action_required")] | first | .conclusion // "") as $c
                   | ([.workflow_runs[] | select(.status != "completed")] | length) as $p
                   | "\($c)|\($p)|\($oldest)"' 2>/dev/null
          }

          while [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$deadline" ]; do
            out="$(poll_api || true)"
            if [ -z "$out" ]; then
              api_fails=$((api_fails + 1))
              if [ "$api_fails" -eq 1 ] || [ $((api_fails % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then
                echo "::warning::dispatch-run poll failed ${api_fails}x (api/jq) — continuing"
              fi
              if [ "$api_fails" -eq 1 ]; then
                note "| :warning: dispatch-watch: run poll failed ${api_fails}x — verdicts may lag reality."
              fi
              sleep 30
              continue
            fi
            c="${out%%|*}"; rest="${out#*|}"; pending="${rest%%|*}"; oldest="${rest##*|}"
            age=0
            if [ "$pending" -gt 0 ]; then age=$(( $(date +%s) - oldest )); fi
            echo "poll: verdict='${c:-none}' pending=$pending pending_age=${age}s (t=${SECONDS}s)"

            # Fast terminal verdicts — red stays red in seconds.
            case "$c" in
              failure|timed_out|startup_failure|action_required)
                echo "conclusion=$c" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                echo "SM-dispatched CI run verdict: $c"
                exit 0 ;;
            esac

            stale=0
            if [ "$pending" -gt 0 ] && [ "$age" -ge "$STALE_PENDING" ]; then stale=1; fi

            # Green: only when nothing is pending, or the pending run is
            # wedged past the staleness cap.
            if [ "$c" = "success" ] && { [ "$pending" -eq 0 ] || [ "$stale" -eq 1 ]; }; then
              if [ "$stale" -eq 1 ]; then
                note "| :warning: dispatched run pending ${age}s (wedged?) — accepted older verdict \`success\`."
                echo "SM-dispatched CI run verdict: success (stale pending ${age}s ignored)"
              else
                echo "SM-dispatched CI run verdict: success"
              fi
              echo "conclusion=success" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi

            # Stale pending with no verdict to fall back on: escalate once,
            # keep polling — the slow-pool signal stays honest.
            if [ "$stale" -eq 1 ] && [ "$escalated" -eq 0 ]; then
              escalated=1
              note "| :warning: dispatched run pending ${age}s with no terminal verdict on \`${ref_display}\` — wedged queue? Polling continues until the deadline."
              echo "::warning::dispatched run pending ${age}s with no terminal verdict — watch continues"
            fi

            sleep 30
          done

          echo "::error::SM-dispatched validation did not conclude within $((WAIT / 60)) min (api failures: ${api_fails}) — SM tick broken or queue stalled"
          note "| :x: dispatch-watch: no verdict within $((WAIT / 60)) min on \`${ref_display}\` — api_failures=${api_fails}. SM tick broken or queue stalled."
          exit 1

  quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    needs: sm-validation
    if: …

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
#
#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      (github.event.inputs.pr != '' &&

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# Explicit top-level permissions, mirroring the pinned factory's own block
# (factory-teammate.yml declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions
# write). A reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the caller, so the
# caller must grant at least what the callee declares — an explicit
# read-only block here made every call fail validation with
# startup_failure (live bisect, 2026-09-18); this mirror is the minimal
# consistent set (SEC-08, #796).
permissions:
  contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
  issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
  actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
  gate:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in
            workflow_dispatch)
              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            issues)
              # Assignment-driven loop: a fresh `assigned` event (human
              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.
              # POLICY (#693 steering): dev fires ONLY when ai-teammate is
              # the sole assignee — any human assignee owns the issue and
              # the machine stands by for reviews instead (review paths:
              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                else
                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
                fi
              else
                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              fi
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
          esac
          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

  factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@8c02d860813f520d8c43af8c56f3f56452153295
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 8c02d860813f520d8c43af8c56f3f56452153295
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}

content.text:
# mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # All nine stages selected = a shared/unknown path changed:
          if [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ]; then
            # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
            stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          fi
          if [ "$(echo $stages | wc -w)" -eq 9 ]; then
            echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #303: the #262 DoD perf gate must red-block the MERGE for
          # trajectory regressions, not only the release — before #551 the
          # only integration leg outside PRs was tag-time. The perf-gate
          # leg re-selects the same gate via --tags perf. Paths = everything
          # the #262 fix touched: ledger core, fa_ui trajectory widgets, CLI
          # trajectory parts, the fah entrypoint, its tests, and the app's
          # session load path.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^lib/src/trajectory/|^packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/|^lib/src/cli/trajectory_|^bin/fah\.dart$|^test/(integration/)?trajectory/|^flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service(_sessions)?\.dart$)'; then
            echo "perf=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
  # only prove the SBPL PROFILE TEXT (unit + guard/profile parity) — the
  # kernel's last-match-wins read/write enforcement of rw mounts under a
  # read-denied prefix needs a real `sandbox-exec` run, which exists only on
  # macOS. Both live suites skip with a NAMED reason wherever they cannot
  # run (no sandbox-exec / already-sandboxed host / HOME outside /Users) —
  # the skip lands in the job log, never silent; this leg is where they
  # actually execute. The leg is a real gate input: `quality-gate` NEEDS it
  # and fails the merge when it fails (a skip — a diff with no core paths —
  # passes, like every other optional leg).
  #
  # Skip condition note (PR #718 review): gating on `core` covers
  # `shared`-only diffs too — the classifier maps a shared/unknown path to
  # ALL nine stages, `test-core` among them, so `core=true` falls out and
  # this leg runs; only docs-only diffs (or non-PR context mismatches)
  # skip it.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  cube-kernel-live:
    name: Cube kernel live (macOS)

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 801
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/801
- **Title**: ci(security): SHA-pinned actions, explicit minimal permissions, dual-graph audit
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-796` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +440
- **Deletions**: -221
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T08:46:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-22T18:30:47Z

## PR Description

Closes #796 (SEC-08, MEDIUM).

## What

1. **SHA-pinned every third-party action ref** in `.github/workflows/*.yml` (213 call sites, 13 distinct actions). Each keeps its moving tag as a trailing comment (`actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`). SHAs resolved from the tag/branch heads live at PR time via the GitHub refs API. First-party repo-relative refs (`./.github/actions/...`) are exempt; the `dmtools-agents` factory `uses:` lines were already SHA-pinned and are byte-identical (machine-sm.yml / ai-teammate.yml touched only where noted below).
   - `ruby/setup-ruby@v1` is a moving BRANCH (no v1 tag exists) — pinned to the branch head `e8944e80` (v1.99 line).
2. **Explicit minimal top-level `permissions:` everywhere** (was implicit in 6 workflows). Jobs needing more keep their existing job-level grants.
   - `ai-teammate.yml`: the old comment forbade a permissions block because a read-only one startup_failure'd every factory call (live bisect 2026-09-18). The factory-teammate.yml (pinned ref) declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions **write**; a reusable workflow cannot raise rights above the caller, so the caller now mirrors exactly those scopes — the minimal consistent set. This is the caller↔reusable consistency the issue asks for; the factory call still validates.
   - `machine-sm.yml` already had a correct mirrored block — untouched.
3. **New `supply-chain` gate job** (every PR, no path gating, part of the aggregate Quality gate):
   - AC1: `scripts/check_action_pins.sh` fails any third-party ref that is not a full commit SHA (digest-pinned `docker://` refs would pass; nothing else).
   - AC2: lint asserts every workflow file has a top-level `permissions:` block (presence, not convention).
   - AC4 (REG): the job writes a `@v4` fixture and asserts the checker REJECTS it, plus a SHA-pinned fixture it must accept. Verified locally: bad fixture exit 1, clean exit 0, repo scan green.
4. **New `dep-audit` matrix job — both dependency graphs** (AC3):
   - `hosted`: `pubspec.yaml` alone — what `pub publish` ships and pub.dev consumers resolve;
   - `vendored`: `pubspec.yaml` + `pubspec_overrides.yaml` — local/CI/release binaries (dart_tui rides `vendor/dart_tui`).
   - The split is documented in the job summary; each leg also asserts from the resolved `pubspec.lock` that dart_tui actually came from its own source (`source: hosted` vs `source: path`), so a silently-collapsed split fails the leg. Both legs join the aggregate Quality gate.

## Verification

- All 21 workflow YAMLs parse (ruby yaml); `bash -n` clean on the new script.
- `bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh` → OK over the full tree (workflows + composite actions).
- Fixture REG run locally: `@v4` fixture fails (exit 1), SHA-pinned fixture passes, repo scan passes.
- AC2 lint loop over all workflows: no missing blocks.

## Notes / gaps

- Dependabot/Renovate is listed in the issue contract ("keeps them current") but this repo has no package-ecosystem config for actions and adding one was not requested in the Change scope — the trailing tag comments make manual bumping a one-liner; happy to add a `github-actions` Dependabot config as a follow-up if wanted.
- `actions/upload-artifact@v7` (build-macos.yml) and the other major versions were pinned as-found; upgrades are a separate concern.

    "summary": "ci(security): SHA-pinned actions, explicit minimal permissions, dual-graph audit",
    "description": "Closes #796 (SEC-08, MEDIUM).

## What

1. **SHA-pinned every third-party action ref** in `.github/workflows/*.yml` (213 call sites, 13 distinct actions). Each keeps its moving tag as a trailing comment (`actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`). SHAs resolved from the tag/branch heads live at PR time via the GitHub refs API. First-party repo-relative refs (`./.github/actions/...`) are exempt; the `dmtools-agents` factory `uses:` lines were already SHA-pinned and are byte-identical (machine-sm.yml / ai-teammate.yml touched only where noted below).
   - `ruby/setup-ruby@v1` is a moving BRANCH (no v1 tag exists) — pinned to the branch head `e8944e80` (v1.99 line).
2. **Explicit minimal top-level `permissions:` everywhere** (was implicit in 6 workflows). Jobs needing more keep their existing job-level grants.
   - `ai-teammate.yml`: the old comment forbade a permissions block because a read-only one startup_failure'd every factory call (live bisect 2026-09-18). The factory-teammate.yml (pinned ref) declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions **write**; a reusable workflow cannot raise rights above the caller, so the caller now mirrors exactly those scopes — the minimal consistent set. This is the caller↔reusable consistency the issue asks for; the factory call still validates.
   - `machine-sm.yml` already had a correct mirrored block — untouched.
3. **New `supply-chain` gate job** (every PR, no path gating, part of the aggregate Quality gate):
   - AC1: `scripts/check_action_pins.sh` fails any third-party ref that is not a full commit SHA (digest-pinned `docker://` refs would pass; nothing else).
   - AC2: lint asserts every workflow file has a top-level `permissions:` block (presence, not convention).
   - AC4 (REG): the job writes a `@v4` fixture and asserts the checker REJECTS it, plus a SHA-pinned fixture it must accept. Verified locally: bad fixture exit 1, clean exit 0, repo scan green.
4. **New `dep-audit` matrix job — both dependency graphs** (AC3):
   - `hosted`: `pubspec.yaml` alone — what `pub publish` ships and pub.dev consumers resolve;
   - `vendored`: `pubspec.yaml` + `pubspec_overrides.yaml` — local/CI/release binaries (dart_tui rides `vendor/dart_tui`).
   - The split is documented in the job summary; each leg also asserts from the resolved `pubspec.lock` that dart_tui actually came from its own source (`source: hosted` vs `source: path`), so a silently-collapsed split fails the leg. Both legs join the aggregate Quality gate.

## Verification

- All 21 workflow YAMLs parse (ruby yaml); `bash -n` clean on the new script.
- `bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh` → OK over the full tree (workflows + composite actions).
- Fixture REG run locally: `@v4` fixture fails (exit 1), SHA-pinned fixture passes, repo scan passes.
- AC2 lint loop over all workflows: no missing blocks.

## Notes / gaps

- Dependabot/Renovate is listed in the issue contract ("keeps them current") but this repo has no package-ecosystem config for actions and adding one was not requested in the Change scope — the trailing tag comments make manual bumping a one-liner; happy to add a `github-actions` Dependabot config as a follow-up if wanted.
- `actions/upload-artifact@v7` (build-macos.yml) and the other major versions were pinned as-found; upgrades are a separate concern."
